title: Why Won't a Raw Egg Stay Stopped? #kitchenscience #physics
description:
Spin a raw egg and a hard-boiled egg on a table. Stop each one for a moment with a fingertip, then let go. The boiled egg stays still. The raw egg starts turning again. Your finger only stopped the shell. The runny white and yolk inside were never stopped, so they keep swirling, and when you let go, their friction against the shell drags it back around. A hard-boiled egg is solid: shell, white and yolk move as one body, so it all stops at once. It is a way to tell a raw egg from a boiled one without cracking it.
